messages:
Dana: :rotating_light: Heads up — eu-west1 preemptible GPU pool is flapping. Seen ~6 nodes go NotReady and get NoSchedule over the last 30m. Affected: preemptible-gpu-low-latency.
Ryan: Which zone? Any autoscaler events that line up?
Dana: eu-west1-b/c. Autoscaler did a burst at 09:12 UTC and 09:25 UTC. Seems to coincide with a large batch job.
Elaine: Pasting short kubectl and device-plugin output from one affected node:```
$ kubectl get nodes | grep gpu
preempt-gpu-7q2k   NotReady,SchedulingDisabled   2d   v1.28.3
preempt-gpu-9l8m   Ready                          1h   v1.28.3

$ kubectl describe node preempt-gpu-7q2k | grep -A3 Taints
Taints: node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable:NoSchedule

$ journalctl -u nvidia-device-plugin -n 50 --no-pager
Sep 15 09:27:12 preempt-gpu-7q2k nvidia-device-plugin[2345]: panic: registerEnt failed: already registered resource name: nvidia.com/gpu
Sep 15 09:27:12 preempt-gpu-7q2k nvidia-device-plugin[2345]: goroutine 1 [running]:
Sep 15 09:27:12 preempt-gpu-7q2k nvidia-device-plugin[2345]: main.main()
Sep 15 09:27:12 preempt-gpu-7q2k systemd[1]: nvidia-device-plugin.service: main process exited, code=exited, status=2/INVALIDARG
```
Dennis: That "already registered resource name" screams duplicate registration. Did the node-init add device-plugin twice or are there two daemonsets?
Priya: We only run one daemonset in rho-cluster, but preemptible image runs our legacy init script that used to install a vendor device-plugin for older drivers during baking. If the image includes baked plugin + our daemonset it would register twice on boot.
Dana: Confirmed — checked /var/lib/kubelet/plugins and found both `/opt/vendor/nvidia-device-plugin` (baked) and `/var/lib/kubelet/ds/nvidia-device-plugin` from the daemonset. When the autoscaler rapidly creates instances the baked plugin sometimes comes up first, then daemonset comes up and fails to register -> device-plugin exits and kubelet taints node NoSchedule.
Ryan: Oof. So the race is: baked plugin registers, daemonset can't register, crashes -> kubelet sees plugin failure and marks node? Is there a kubelet behavior that taints on device-plugin failure?
Elaine: We've seen kubelet mark nodes NotReady when critical resource registration fails (GPU capacity reported as zero). In this case the operator path we use in startup marks schedulingDisabled to prevent GPU workloads.
Dennis: Short fix: cordon the preemptible pool and stop autoscaler for that pool, roll an image without the baked plugin. Long fix: update init to check for existing plugin and skip, or add a startup check in the daemonset to wait for a free name.
Priya: I'll push a canary AMI without the baked plugin to eu-west and create a new nodepool with scale-up disabled for testing.
Dana: Can someone cordon/drain the currently flaky nodes so we don't get cascading evictions?
Ryan: On it — cordoned preemptible-gpu-low-latency and draining non-critical batch pods.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0915-42 (tracking preemptible GPU registration race in eu-west1). Assigned: eng-infra / infra-sre.
Dana: Thanks — next steps: (1) Priya create canary nodepool w/ cleaned AMI, (2) Dennis add init-check to skip baked plugin if daemonset exists, (3) Elaine add a readiness gate to the daemonset so it won't exit on duplicate register (defensive), (4) disable autoscaler for pool until canary validated. I'll update the incident with timelines. :thumbsup:
Priya: Will do. ETA for canary ~1.5h.
Dennis: I'll open a small PR for the init check, should be quick.
Elaine: I'll add an alert rule to detect duplicate plugin installs across /var/lib/kubelet/plugins and fire before autoscaler bursts.
Dana: Good. We'll keep this thread for updates and close when stable.
